QUESTION: What are the basic safety equipment a person should wear when operating the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Wear appropriate eye and ear protection and safety shoes; always use safety glasses (with side shields) while operating the machine. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf] [003__L1__Safety_Recommendations__pp3-8.pdf]

QUESTION: If an electrical fault is detected, what is the appropriate action for the person operating the HAAS Lathe to do?
STUDENT ANSWER: Stop machine operation and do not run the machine until the electrical fault condition is corrected. Inspect and correct the electrical condition (for example: clear clogged air filters/restore fan cooling for electronics overheat; correct incoming voltage for low/high voltage faults). If you cannot clear or correct the alarm, contact your Haas Factory Outlet (HFO) for service. [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf] [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

QUESTION: If after I powered on the HAAS Lathe, I want to change the program that will run, how can I do so?

Basic procedure (using a USB device or network):

- In the Select Device popup choose the destination device/directory, navigate into the desired directory ([RIGHT] to enter), and press [ENTER] to complete the copy. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; lower pressure can make the tailstock unreliable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- HPU oil problems — low HPU oil level or high HPU oil temperature can affect hydraulic operation (HPU oil low / HPU oil temperature icons appear when these conditions exist). [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf]

- Power interruption while engaged — if power was lost while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock before resuming. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock not locked or improperly positioned (ST-10) — the ST-10 must be positioned manually and the tailstock body locked before applying the quill; failure to do so can cause problems or collisions. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage / creeping — tailstock position can change over time if left partially retracted or not in contact with the workpiece due to hydraulic leakage. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Control inputs/sequence issues — note that [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion (you must press [RESET] or [EMERGENCY STOP]); this can give the appearance of improper function if expecting feed-hold to stop tailstock motion. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If none of these conditions are present, the cause cannot be determined from the provided documents.

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: The tailstock could have low PSI. PSI below 120 is not enough. If you have followed the tailstock operating procedure correctly and there is clearly a violation, you should contact HAAS support.
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; lower pressure can make the tailstock unreliable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- HPU oil problems — low HPU oil level or high HPU oil temperature can affect hydraulic operation (HPU oil low / HPU oil temperature icons appear when these conditions exist). [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf]

- Power interruption while engaged — if power was lost while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock before resuming. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock not locked or improperly positioned (ST-10) — the ST-10 must be positioned manually and the tailstock body locked before applying the quill; failure to do so can cause problems or collisions. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage / creeping — tailstock position can change over time if left partially retracted or not in contact with the workpiece due to hydraulic leakage. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Control inputs/sequence issues — note that [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion (you must press [RESET] or [EMERGENCY STOP]); this can give the appearance of improper function if expecting feed-hold to stop tailstock motion. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If none of these conditions are present, the cause cannot be determined from the provided documents.

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can change/load tools on a Haas lathe using the machine’s tool-change methods and G-code tool calls described in the documentation:

- Tool Change Method (automatic, Gang T1, or T1 Post/manual): Setting 113 selects how a tool change is executed — Auto uses the machine’s automatic tool changer; Gang Tl changes only tool offsets (examples: T12, T1213, T1200); Tl Post stops for a manual tool load and resumes when you load the spindle and press [CYCLE START]. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Standard tool call: Use a Tnn (or Tnnnn) code to select the tool and its offset before the tool-change line (typical practice shown throughout the examples). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__12__6.11_More_Information_Online__pp276-278.pdf] [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- G200 “Index on the Fly” (fast turret tool change): G200 performs unclamp → incremental U/W move → tool change → rapid back to the programmed X/Z. Example syntax: G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2. Use caution and proof at reduced feedrates; ensure U/W offsets are safe for current position. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- Tool setting/probing (G211/G212): Use G211 (manual tool setting) or G212 (auto re-probe) with required T and H parameters to set or re-measure tool offsets using the automatic tool probe; the probe must be calibrated first and a tool/offset must be called for G212. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

If you need a specific command sequence for your machine or for a side-mount changer/turret model, consult the example program lines and your machine’s tool-changer option documentation. The cited files above contain examples and cautions for each method.

QUESTION: I've noticed that the corners of my machined parts look too sharp on all my programs. Can I change this on the HAAS Lathe?

- A higher value lets the control feed faster around corners but may round them up to the specified tolerance. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

Supporting details:
- Pressing [HANDLE JOG] enters Jog mode; the handle selects the increment and moves the selected axis (you can also enter an axis letter then press [HANDLE JOG] to select that axis) [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf].  
- Setting 104 lets the handle single-step through a program (reverse direction generates a feed hold) if enabled [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf].

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: The Run‑Stop‑Jog‑Continue feature lets you stop a running program, jog the axes away from the part, and then restart the program. To use it: press [FEED HOLD] (axis motion stops, spindle keeps turning), press the axis key (X, Y or Z) and then press [HANDLE JOG]; the control stores the current X, Y, and Z positions and you may jog the X, Y and Z axes in this mode. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Potential benefits (as stated/implied by the feature):
- Lets you pause a run to move the tool away from the workpiece for inspection or to clear an interference without stopping the spindle. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Maintains stored positions so the program can be resumed accurately after jogging. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I install a collet on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: The provided documents do not include a single “collet installation” procedure, but relevant instructions are in the maintenance and live-tooling sections:

Standard collet/collet-screw service (Collet aligning screw removal/install):
- Mark a reference line on the quill and nose cap. Remove set screw “R”, unscrew nose cap “S”, remove lock screw “T” and collet aligning screw “U”. Replace “U”, insert the collet and check the dog on the end of the screw does not interfere with the guide slot. Replace lock screw “T”, replace nose cap “S” and check alignment with the felt-pen marks, then replace set screw “R”. Check gap “V” = .003" (0.08 mm). Do not remove the nose cap before removing set screw “R” (CAUTION). [008__Chapter_3_-_Maintenance__pp49-62.pdf]

Live-tool ER collet (ER-32-AN) assembly and tightening (for live-tool holders—do not tighten these collets on the turret):
- Insert the tool bit into the ER-AN nut insert and thread the nut insert into the collet housing. Place the ER-32-AN tube wrench over the tool bit and hand-tighten the nut insert using the tube wrench. Place Spanner 1 over the pin and lock it against the collet housing nut, then engage the tube-wrench teeth with Spanner 2 and tighten. IMPORTANT: Never tighten live-tool collets while the toolholder is on the turret — doing so will damage the machine. [006__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

If you need a separate step-by-step “install collet in turret/toolholder” procedure (torques, mounting-bolt pattern, precise order for your turret/collet system), that exact procedure is not present in the supplied documents.

QUESTION: How do I power up the HAAS lathe?

Power-up procedure:

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum operating pressure for hydraulic tailstocks (ST-20/30) is 120 psi; below this the tailstock may not function reliably [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf].  
- Incorrect HPU pressure setting — tailstock hold force is adjusted at the HPU (except ST-40 uses Setting 241); verify and set pressure per the machine decal and HPU valves [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf] [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__08__4.8_Drawtube_Operation__pp123-123.pdf].  
- Power interruption / lost hold force — if power was interrupted while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, hold force is lost; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock after power is restored [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf].  
- Foot-pedal or control settings disabled — tailstock pedal control can be disabled via Setting 332 (tailstock pedal lockout); check this setting [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf].  
- Using M21/M22 improperly on a manually positioned tailstock — on ST-10 the tailstock is positioned manually and should not be commanded by M21 in a program; the tailstock body must be locked before commanding M21 [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf].  
- Normal hydraulic leakage or check-valve behavior — tailstock position can creep if left partially retracted due to leakage; check valves hold quill position but leakage can still change position over time [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf].

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: You select the desired tool with a T-code and then execute the tool-change action; examples and options in the manual:

- Simple tool call: use a T-code (for example T101) to select the tool and offset before machining (see program examples). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__12__6.11_More_Information_Online__pp276-278.pdf]

- Fast (Index on the Fly) tool change: use G200 with a Tnn and optional U/W (incremental move) and X/Z (final position) to unclamp, shift slightly, change tools, and return to the cut position in one line (e.g. G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2.). Proof programs carefully at slow feed/rapids. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- Control of turret rotation direction: M17/M18 set turret rotation forward or reverse for tool changes; the selection remains in effect for the program. [008__L1__Chapter_8_M-codes__pp365-386__L2__01__8.1_Introduction__pp365-384_part01.pdf]

Supporting notes:
- Live-tool drives automatically turn off on a tool change. For best milling accuracy clamp the spindle before live-tool operations. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]
- The lathe returns the Y axis to spindle centerline after a tool change; ensure turret is correctly positioned before commanding rotation. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__11__6.10_Y_Axis__pp272-275.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Run-Stop-Jog-Continue lets you stop a running program, jog the X, Y, or Z axes away from the part, and then resume the program. To use it: press [FEED HOLD] (axis motion stops, spindle continues), press the axis key (X, Y, or Z) then press [HANDLE JOG] to store current X/Y/Z positions and jog away; when ready, continue the program. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Benefits (from the described behavior)
- Allows removal of the tool from the part during a pause without stopping the spindle, reducing thermal or position disturbance. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Preserves stored X/Y/Z positions so the program can be resumed accurately after jogging. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

The sources do not provide additional performance metrics or other advantages beyond the steps and behavior above.

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can back up the machine data and programs to a removable device (USB) or to the network, then remove seldom-used programs from machine memory. Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to copy files to another device or directory, and to back up machine data. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Steps (Device Manager):
- Press [LIST PROGRAM] to open the Device Manager and select the device tab for the destination (e.g., USB or network). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Use the cursor keys to highlight the file(s) or directory you want to copy; press ENTER to check-mark multiple files. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Press [F2] to start the copy operation, choose the destination device/directory, navigate into the target folder with [RIGHT], then press ENTER to complete the copy. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Notes and safety:
- If you use M98 subprogram calls later, remember subprogram files must be named Onnnnn.nc (include O, leading zeros, and .nc) or be in memory; alternatively set custom search locations (Setting 252) so the control can find subprograms on other devices. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- You can add a directory as a custom subprogram search location via the Device Manager File [F3] menu (Setting 252 add). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf] [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- When creating or copying files to external devices, use the File Name field if you want a specific filename on the storage device. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: I want to change out a tool for a different one on the HAAS Lathe. How do I select the tool I want to switch out on the turret?
STUDENT ANSWER: To select (call) a specific tool and offset for a turret tool change, use the T-code in the form Txxyy (tool number xx and offset/geometry yy) — for example T101 selects tool 1 with offset 01. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]

You can also perform a tool change in MDI by:
- Toggle to MDI mode ([MDI/DNC]) and then index the turret with [TURRET FWD] or [TURRET REV] to move to the next tool; the Active Tool display shows the current tool. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]

Notes/precautions:
- T-codes take the Txxyy format where xx is the tool station number and yy is the tool geometry/wear index (00 = no geometry/wear applied). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]
- There is no X or Z motion required before a tool change, but X/Z must be positioned to a safe location prior to tool change to avoid collisions. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes from the provided documentation:

- Hydraulic pressure set below the recommended minimum (120 psi), which can make the hydraulic tailstock unreliable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Loss of hydraulic power or power interruption while tailstock engaged: if power was shut off or interrupted, the hold force is lost and the workpiece must be supported and the tailstock zero returned before resuming. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage over time causing the tailstock position to change if left partially retracted or not in contact with a workpiece. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- HPU oil level or HPU oil temperature problems (HPU oil low or HPU oil temperature warning icons indicate issues with the hydraulic power unit). Check HPU oil level and temperature. [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf] and [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot pedal or control settings: tailstock pedal control can be disabled (Setting 332) or Setting 145 (Tailstock At Part for [CYCLE START]) may prevent operation if tailstock is not at part. Verify relevant settings. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf] and [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: The lathe tool change process depends on the code/mode you use; common methods shown in the sources:

- Standard/manual tool change (T-call with turret stop): Call the tool with a T code (for example T101) and the turret will change to that tool/offset when the T-code executes. Use safe positioning first (example startup block: G00 G18 G20 G40 G80 G99; T101). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__12__6.11_More_Information_Online__pp276-278.pdf]

- G200 "Index on the Fly" (fast automated tool change without full retract): Use a single G200 line with required T (and optional U, W, X, Z) to unclamp, move incrementally, change tools, and move back in one fast operation. Example: G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2. . CAUTION: proof the program at reduced rapid and ensure tooling/clearances are safe. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- For lathes with automatic tool changers or gang/tool-post modes: Setting 113 (Tool Change Method) selects how a tool change is executed (Auto = automatic tool changer, Gang Tl = gang tool behavior where T12 uses tool 12 offset, Tl Post = manual tool change prompts operator to load the tool and press CYCLE START). Use the selection appropriate to your machine and program. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Additional practical notes from the sources:
- Always include safe startup/preparation blocks (example: G00 G18 G20 G40 G80 G99 before tool calls). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__12__6.11_More_Information_Online__pp276-278.pdf]
- When using G200, beware incremental U/W moves and that the turret moves slightly toward the spindle when unclamping; verify clearances and consider tailstock restricted zone settings to avoid collisions. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- For machines with live tooling or C-axis, ensure relevant M-codes (e.g., M154/M155) and spindle/live-tool commands are used as shown in program examples. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__12__6.11_More_Information_Online__pp276-278.pdf]

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The HAAS documentation includes specific chuck safety warnings: do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed (higher speeds reduce clamping force), unsupported barstock must not extend outside the drawtube, chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the chuck diameter, do not machine parts larger than the chuck, and improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force. It also instructs to grease the chuck weekly and follow the chuck manufacturer’s service and workholding warnings, and to set hydraulic pressure correctly to hold the workpiece without distortion. QUESTION: I've noticed that the corners of my machined parts look too sharp on all my programs. Can I change this on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. You can have the control round corners by increasing the Maximum Corner Rounding (Setting 85), which defines the machining accuracy tolerance around corners; a larger value allows the control to round corners up to that radius and can increase feedrate through corners. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

- If Setting 85 is zero, the control acts as if exact stop is active (no corner rounding). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to copy or save files and to back up machine data. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

How to do it (summary from the device manager instructions):
- Press [LIST PROGRAM] to open the Device Manager and select the device tab for your destination (e.g., USB). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- In the file list, place a check mark on the programs/files you want to save (press ENTER in the leftmost check box). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Press [F2] to start the copy operation, choose the destination device/directory, navigate into the target directory (use [RIGHT] to enter), then press [ENTER] to complete the copy. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Notes and tips from the manual:

If you need step-by-step guidance for backing up full machine data (not just program files), the Device Manager includes functions to back up and restore machine data—use those menus to save complete machine data to USB or network locations. QUESTION: I want to change out a tool for a different one on the HAAS Lathe. How do I select the tool I want to switch out on the turret?

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes based on the documentation:

- Hydraulic pressure too low (below recommended minimum 120 psi for hydraulic tailstocks ST-20/30), causing unreliable tailstock function. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Hold force/pressure not set correctly at the HPU (adjust tailstock/quill hold force at the HPU; ST-10 and ST-20/30 use HPU valves). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Hydraulic leakage causing tailstock position drift when left partially retracted or not in contact (normal system leakage can change position over time). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock engaged at power loss: if power was interrupted while tailstock engaged, hold force is lost and the workpiece must be supported and the tailstock zero returned to resume; failure to follow startup procedure may appear as malfunction. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- For ST-40 servo tailstock: incorrect Setting 241 (Tailstock Hold Force) could be wrong, or the control does not know tailstock position until zero return after power loss—this can prevent expected motion. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf; 009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Tailstock foot pedal disabled by Setting 332/332 (Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut / Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut appears as Setting 332 and 332/331 naming in sources) — if the pedal is ignored, tailstock won't respond to pedal. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf; 009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Using M21 when tailstock is manually positioned (ST-10): issuing M21 with a manually positioned tailstock can cause unsafe or unexpected motion—document cautions against this. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If these items do not explain the failure, the provided documents do not give further troubleshooting steps.

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: The manual describes two common tool change methods on Haas lathes:

- Automatic tool changer (Auto): load/changes are performed automatically by the machine’s tool changer. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Manual (Tl Post): when Setting 113 is set to Tl Post the control stops at a tool change and prompts you to load the tool; after you load the spindle you press [CYCLE START] to continue the program. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Additional relevant notes from the sources:
- “Gang Tl” (a selection of Setting 113) implements gang-tool behavior by switching tool offsets only (e.g., T12 uses offset from tool 12, T1213 uses offset from 13, T1200 uses no tool offset). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- Live tooling automatically turns off when a tool change is commanded; for best milling accuracy clamp the spindle with the spindle clamp M-codes before machining. Maximum live-tool speed is 6000 RPM. (See Live Tooling installation and M-codes). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf] [008__L1__Chapter_8_M-codes__pp365-386__L2__01__8.1_Introduction__pp365-384_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The HAAS documentation includes multiple specific safety warnings for the chuck:

- Danger: Improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; higher speeds reduce chuck clamping force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Unsupported barstock must not extend outside the drawtube. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Grease the chuck weekly and follow the chuck manufacturer’s regular service instructions. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the diameter of the chuck; do not machine parts larger than the chuck. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Follow all chuck manufacturer warnings regarding the chuck and workholding procedures; hydraulic pressure must be set correctly to hold the workpiece without distortion. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Reduce spindle speed when performing dangerous operations (e.g., turning oversized or marginally clamped parts) to protect the operator and enclosure. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Setting 283 / 284 / 281-related controls affect chuck/unclamp behavior and safety (e.g., Main Spindle Chuck Unclamp RPM and foot-pedal lockout). Review Settings 281–284 for chuck-related limits and lockouts. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

(See the “Chuck safety” section and related settings in 001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf and the settings references in 009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf.)

QUESTION: If I want to make a backup of my HAAS Lathe ATM(Advanced Tool Management) information how do I do so?
STUDENT ANSWER: The control saves ATM (Advanced Tool Management) data as macro variables and tool tables which you back up like other machine data: save the relevant files to a USB device or User Data via the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) or Net Share. The control’s backup/save procedures (save/load) use the Device Manager and USB/Net Share functions. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf] [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]

Supporting details:
- ATM data is referenced by macro/tool variables (e.g., #8500–#8564 relate to ATM tool group and tool fields) and global macro ranges; these variables are saved/loaded through Net Share or USB like settings and offsets. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]
- Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to copy files between machine memory and USB (select files with check marks, then press F2 to copy to the destination device). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: I keep noticing my HAAS Lathe air reservoir has too much condensation in it. Is there any way to fix this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. Adjust the condensate purge interval and duration settings so the air reservoir purges more often and/or for longer.

- Setting 242 (Air Water Purge Interval) specifies the interval, in minutes, between condensate purges from the system air reservoir. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- Setting 243 (Air Water Purge On-Time) specifies the duration, in seconds, of condensate purges from the system air reservoir. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Increase the interval frequency (decrease the minutes in Setting 242) and/or increase the on-time (seconds in Setting 243) to remove more condensate. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

QUESTION: I want to make a change to a program on the HAAS Lathe, but also keep the current version in case I mess something up. What can I do?

- If you later want to revert to the last saved version, use Discard Changes to revert the file to its previously saved state. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

- Additional safeguards:
  - You can use UNDO to reverse recent edits (up to 40 edits) but not after leaving EDIT:EDIT mode. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can free space by backing up programs and data to an external storage location, then removing them from the machine memory.

- Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to load, transfer, and back up data, including copying programs to a USB memory device or other connected devices. This lets you store current machine information and programs off the control and remove rarely used ones from memory. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]
- Connect a USB memory device and use the Device Manager to copy the desired programs to the USB device, then delete or clear them from memory as needed. You can also back up your active program and other data before removing items to regain space. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]

Notes:
- The device manager shows memory devices (including USB) and allows saving/loading and backing up machine data. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]
- If you need to retrieve items later, copy them back from the USB device to memory. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I power up the HAAS lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Powering up the lathe involves a sequence starting from a powered-on control pendant and completing with the machine in OPERATION:MEM mode.

- Ensure the area around crash hazards (tool probe, parts catcher, tailstock, tool turret, secondary spindle) is clear. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-103.pdf]
- Press POWER ON until you see the Haas logo and the display shows the startup screen. Then dismiss the startup screen if needed. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-103.pdf]
- Turn the EMERGENCY STOP to the right to reset, then press RESET to clear startup alarms. If alarms cannot be cleared, contact your Haas Factory Outlet. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-103.pdf]
- If the machine is enclosed, close the doors. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-103.pdf]
- Press POWER UP. The Zero All Axes display shows; select the axis zero return order. The control is now in OPERATION:MEM mode. You can press CYCLE START to run the active program. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-103.pdf]

Notes from the pendant:
- The control pendant front panel provides the POWER ON and POWER OFF controls used during power sequencing. [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes and quick checks:

- Hydraulic pressure too low or leaking: The ST-20/30 tailstock requires a minimum operating pressure of 120 psi to function reliably; check and adjust the hydraulic pressure at the HPU, and verify the hold force as indicated on the machine decal. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Hold force not maintained after power or during interruption: If power was interrupted, the hold force is lost and you must zero return the tailstock before resuming; after power is restored, you may need to edit the program to remove M22 until the tailstock is re-established. - Tailstock not engaged or not at part: Ensure the tailstock is engaged with the workpiece (tailstock hold) and that you are not attempting to jog or move it when it is engaged; verify the tailstock is properly locked and that you are using the correct M-codes (M21/M22) or foot pedal sequence as applicable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption recovery actions: If the tailstock was engaged and power was lost, the control may require zero return and possible program edits before continuing; consult the procedure around Tailstock Zero Return and Safe Restart. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: The HAAS machine can do a full machine backup, which copies the settings, programs, and other data so it's easy to restore later on. To do this you can plug in a USB, navigate to it in the program list, press [F4] and select "Back Up Machine" in the appearing drop down menu. Then from there follow the on screen instructions and choose what you want backed up. You can then restore this backup later on if you need something back.
STUDENT ANSWER: You can offload older programs and machine data to an external USB device (or another memory device) and delete them from the local memory to free space, then store them back when needed.

How to do it (high level steps):
- Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to copy programs to a USB memory device or another memory device, freeing space on the control. The Device Manager shows how to select a destination and perform a copy operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]
- To offload, select the desired programs, press F2 (copy), choose the destination device/directory, then complete the operation. The manual covers the copy process and selecting devices. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]
- You can relocate where subprograms are searched from by Settings 251 (Subprogram Search Location) with options Memory, USB Device, or Setting 252; this lets you point where older subprograms reside, enabling easier offloading without changing all references. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- If you need a storage location to persist after removal from local memory, you can enable a custom subprogram search location (Setting 252) and add that USB path as a location. See the Setting 252 add/remove instructions. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Notes:

- Avoid overwriting macro/reserved O-number ranges when creating or copying programs; follow the guidance in the Device Manager section. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)_pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes and checks for hydraulic tailstock not functioning:

- Hydraulic pressure too low: The recommended minimum operating pressure is 120 psi. If pressure is lower, the tailstock may not function reliably. Check and adjust at the HPU to the correct hold pressure. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Hold pressure lost after power interruption: If power to the lathe was interrupted, the hold force can be lost and you may need to zero return the tailstock before resuming. Ensure power is restored and perform a zero return as needed. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock not in the proper position or away from part: The tailstock must be properly engaged (manual lock or proper retract/advance) and within the programmed range. Check that the tailstock is correctly positioned and not requiring retraction/advancement beyond its current command. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Restricted zone or collision risk: If settings 93 (X clearance) and 94 (Z/B separation) create a restricted zone too tight, tool/turret motions could prevent tailstock engagement or cause crashes. Review the restricted zone settings and test limits after changes. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Manual positioning vs. M21/M22 commands: If the tailstock is manually positioned, using M21/M22 commands in a program can cause unexpected motion. Ensure you’re not issuing M21 in a program when the tailstock is manually positioned. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If issues persist, verify the hydraulic system pressure, confirm no power interruptions, and review tailstock-related settings and safety notes in the tailstock section. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Based on the provided Haas lathe documentation:

- The hydraulic tailstock in ST-20/30 requires a minimum operating pressure of 120 psi for reliable function. If pressure is lower, the tailstock may not function properly. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Ensure the hydraulic pressure is correctly adjusted at the HPU to the required hold force for ST-20/30 (and ST-20/30/40 variants). Refer to the machine decal for the correct hold force setting. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- If power is interrupted while the hydraulic tailstock is engaged, the hold force is lost and you must zero return the tailstock to resume operation; after restoration, you may need to resume with caution and possibly edit the program to remove M22 tailstock motion commands until a proper zero return is performed. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.4_ST-20/30__Tailstock_Operation.pdf]

- The ST-10 tailstock is manually positioned and cannot be moved by M-codes like M21/M22 during normal operation; ensure correct manual locking and check for collisions during movement. If applicable, verify that you are using the correct tailstock type for your model (ST-10 vs ST-20/30/40). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.2_ST-10_Tailstock_Operation.pdf] 

If you provide your exact model (ST-10 vs ST-20/30/40) and whether you’ve recently had a power interruption or changed hydraulic settings, I can narrow down the likely cause further. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?

- In Device Manager, create or select a USB memory device as the destination and copy selected programs (using the Copy operation) to free space on the machine. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- If needed, set up a network or secondary storage path via the Setting 252 / Setting 251 workflows to point backups to removable storage. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Note: The documents describe backing up and transferring programs using the Device Manager and USB/network options; they do not specify a non-permanent internal storage option beyond using external storage via USB or network shares. QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Based on the provided documents, here are practical checks and likely causes to investigate for a hydraulic tailstock issue on a HAAS lathe:

- Check tailstock type and operation notes: Ensure you are using the correct tailstock type (hydraulic quill, hydraulic positioned, or servo) for your model, as each type has different operation characteristics. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Verify hydraulic hold pressure and settings:
  - For hydraulic tailstock (ST-20/30), hold force is set by hydraulic pressure at the HPU; the recommended starting pressure is at least 120 psi for reliable operation. If the pressure is too low, the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.3_Hydraulic_Tailstock__pp109.pdf]
  - For ST-40 servo tailstock, hold force is set via Setting 241 (Tailstock Hold Force). Ensure the correct setting and range are used. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.4_ST-40_Servo_Tailstock__pp110.pdf]
- Check pneumatic/hydraulic interlocks and safety:
  - Tailstock may require a minimum hydraulic pressure to function; if pressure is below spec, movement may be unreliable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.3_Hydraulic_Tailstock__pp109.pdf]

- Restart and power interruption considerations:
  - If power is interrupted, the tailstock hold force may be lost; you must reinitialize the tailstock (zero return) before resuming, and ensure no M22 tailstock retract commands are in effect when restarting a cycle. [4.11.3 ST-20/30], [4.11.4 ST-40 Servo Tailstock], [Tailstock restart notes in 4.11.4]

- Check that you are not attempting to jog or move the tailstock manually in a way that conflicts with the machine’s safety zones (Restricted Zone) or with program commands, which can prevent proper tailstock engagement. [4.11.8 Tailstock Restricted Zone], [4.11.9 Jogging the Tailstock]

- Ensure the tailstock is properly retracted or engaged at the correct location before starting cycles; improper positioning can cause non-functioning tailstock behavior. [4.11.7 Tailstock Foot Pedal Operation], [4.11.2 ST-10 Tailstock Operation]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Run‑Stop‑Jog‑Continue lets you pause a running program, jog the X/Y/Z axes away from the part, and then resume the program. Notes/limitations:

- In EDIT:EDIT mode the control does not automatically save changes as you edit; use MEMORY (or Save/Set To Run in the File menu) to save when you are ready. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include hydraulic pressure, power/state, settings, or alarms:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; adjust pressure at the HPU and refer to the machine decal for quill hold force vs pressure [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf].  
- Loss of hold force after power interruption — if power was lost while the tailstock was engaged the hold force is lost; support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock before resuming (ST-20/30) or note the servo brake behavior and zero return requirements for ST-40 before using M22 commands (ST-20/30/40 procedures) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf].  
- Tailstock foot pedal disabled or lockout — Setting 332 (Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut) can disable pedal input; verify this setting [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf].  
- Foot-pedal alarm behavior — Setting 322 can cause an alarm if the foot pedal is used to move to the hold point and no part is detected; this may prevent normal tailstock operation [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf].  
- Hydraulic system faults or HPU issues — check HPU oil level/temperature and HPU-related warnings/icons (HPU Oil Low / HPU Oil Temperature) on the control which indicate HPU problems that can affect tailstock function [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf].

If these items do not explain the fault, the provided documents do not give further diagnostic steps.

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can perform a tool change on a Haas lathe using either the machine’s tool-change method (Setting 113) or the rapid “Index on the Fly” G200 command; use probe codes (G211/G212) for setting tool offsets. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf] [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

Supporting details:
- Tool-change mode: Setting 113 selects Auto (automatic tool changer), Gang T1 (gang-style offset changes), or T1 Post (manual tool change that stops and prompts you to load the tool, then press CYCLE START). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- Fast tool change: Use G200 Tnnn with optional U/W (incremental retract), and final X/Z positions to unclamp, move incrementally, change the turret, and rapid back to the part in one line (example: G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2.). Proof-run at slow rapids and ensure tools/jaws aren’t contacting the turret path. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- Tool setting/probing: Use G211 (Manual Tool Setting) or G212 (Auto Tool Setting) with required T and H codes to set or re-probe tool offsets (probe must be calibrated first; call Tnnn before G212). Take care with back-working tools to avoid hitting the spindle or back wall. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The manual gives specific chuck safety warnings and precautions, including a DANGER that improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force, and these requirements: do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; grease the chuck weekly per manufacturer instructions; chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the chuck diameter; do not machine parts larger than the chuck; set hydraulic pressure correctly to hold the workpiece without distortion; and reduce spindle speed for dangerous operations (e.g., oversized or marginally clamped parts). [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

QUESTION: A client wants us to measure all out movements in MM instead of Inches. Can the HAAS Lathe also reflect this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. Set Setting 9 (Dimensioning) to MM to make the control use millimeters; all offset values are converted and the default G-code becomes G21. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

Additional notes:
- Changing Setting 9 does not automatically convert a stored program’s numeric axis values — you must update program coordinates for the new units. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]
- Jog increment behavior changes in MM mode (e.g., the first jog increment is multiplied by ten when in MM). [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: I've noticed that the corners of my machined parts look too sharp on all my programs. Can I change this on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. Change Setting 85 (Maximum Corner Rounding) to control how much the control may round corners—raising the value allows larger corner radii (faster feed through corners), lowering it forces tighter corners (slower feed). The default is 0.05". [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

- A higher Setting 85 lets the control round corners up to that tolerance (faster), a lower value slows feed to meet a smaller radius. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]  
- If Setting 85 = 0, the control acts as if Exact Stop is active for each motion block (no rounding). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

- Press the axis key ([X], [Y], or [Z]) then press [HANDLE JOG] — the control stores the current X, Y, Z positions and lets you jog that axis (only X, Y, and Z can be jogged in this mode). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Stated capability/benefit in the documentation:
- The feature “lets you stop a running program, jog away from the part, and then start the program again.” [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Related UI indication:
- The control displays jog/return icons during a run‑stop‑jog‑continue operation to indicate the return and jog states. [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf]

- Press [LIST PROGRAM] to open the Device Manager, navigate to the directory that contains the programs you want to back up. Use the cursor keys and [RIGHT]/[LEFT] to enter/exit directories. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; adjust pressure at the HPU. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption while tailstock engaged — hold force is lost on power loss; support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock after power is restored. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock foot pedal disabled — Setting 332 (Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut) can ignore pedal input when ON. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Foot-pedal alarm configuration — Setting 322 can generate an alarm if the foot pedal moves the tailstock to the hold point and no part is found. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Loose/unlocked tailstock body (ST‑10) — the ST‑10 tailstock body must be locked in place before commanding M21; otherwise motion/holding may be incorrect. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Hydraulic leakage or check‑valve behavior — normal hydraulic leakage can let the tailstock position change over time; check valves hold position but leakage or incorrect valve/HPU settings can cause problems. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Change the active tool with a T-code (for example T101 or T202) on a tool-change line; the turret executes the tool change using the called tool number/offset. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__03__5.3_Tips_and_Tricks__pp147-150.pdf]

- To speed tool changes use G200 (Index on the Fly): G200 Tnnn U... W... X... Z... will unclamp the turret, move incrementally (U/W), perform the tool change, then rapid to the specified X/Z position. Proof programs at low rapid (5% rapid) and keep tools clear of jaws/collet because the turret moves slightly toward the spindle when unclamping. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- If using the Automatic Tool Probe:
  - Use G211 (Manual Tool Setting) to set an initial tool offset (requires a Tnnn and Hnnn; probe must be calibrated first). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
  - Use G212 (Auto Tool Setting) to re-probe a tool with an existing offset (requires a Tnnn called before G212 and correct H tip-direction; misuse can crash a back-working tool). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- Settings that affect tool change behavior:
  - Setting 113 selects the Tool Change Method (Auto, Gang Tl, Tool Post). If set to Tl Post, the machine will stop and prompt the operator to manually load the tool. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Live tooling note: the live-tool drive automatically turns off when a tool change is commanded; torque and mounting instructions apply when installing live-tool holders (do not overtighten collets on the turret). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

QUESTION: I've noticed that the corners of my machined parts look too sharp on all my programs. Can I change this on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. Use Setting 85 “Maximum Corner Rounding” to change how the control handles corners — it defines the machining tolerance (default 0.05") and limits how large corner radii can be. - The control stores axis positions, enabling accurate return to the program’s previously stored coordinates for continuation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- The pendant displays a “Jog” icon during the return portion of a run-stop-jog-continue operation, giving visual feedback of the mode state. [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf]

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can back up your machine data and programs to a removable device (for example a USB memory device) or to files on the connected network using the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]). Use [LIST PROGRAM] to view available devices (Memory, USB Device, network, etc.), select files/programs, and copy them to your destination. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

How to do it (summary of steps):
- Press [LIST PROGRAM] to open the Device Manager and select the source device/tab that contains the programs you want to archive. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Use the cursor keys to highlight files or directories; press [ENTER] to place a check mark in the file selection check box for single or multiple files. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Press F2 to start the copy operation, choose the destination device/directory (USB or network) in the Select Device popup, enter the destination directory with the [RIGHT] key, and press [ENTER] to complete the copy. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Notes and tips from the manual:
- If you copy a program from Memory to a non-memory device, you can assign an optional File Name before copying; programs in non‑memory devices will use that filename (for example Onnnnn.nc). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- You can also back up machine data (machine data backup) via the Device Manager—use the same copy/export procedures to move settings and data to the removable or networked device. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- For subprogram search behavior when running M98 later: if a subprogram is not in memory the control looks for a filename Onnnnn.nc (O with leading zeros and .nc). If you plan to run archived subprograms from removable storage later, keep that naming convention. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

If you want to free space safely, after copying/backup you can delete the rarely used files from machine Memory using the Device Manager’s Delete or check-mark + Delete functions. Follow the same file-selection steps and use F3 → Delete or the DELETE key to remove selected files. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I power up the HAAS lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: 1. Make sure possible crash areas (tool probe, parts catcher, tailstock, tool turret, secondary spindle) are clear. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

2. Press [POWER ON] until the Haas logo appears; after boot, dismiss the startup screen with [CANCEL] if shown. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

3. Turn [EMERGENCY STOP] to the right to reset it. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

4. Press [RESET] to clear startup alarms; if an alarm cannot be cleared, contact your Haas Factory Outlet (HFO). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

5. If the machine is enclosed, close the doors. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

6. Press [POWER UP]. The Zero All Axes display appears; select the axis zero return order. When complete, the control will be in OPERATION:MEM mode and you can press [CYCLE START] to run the active program. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

Additional notes:
- The [POWER ON], [EMERGENCY STOP], [RESET], and [POWER UP] controls are on the pendant front panel. [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf]

If you want to preserve the current MDI text as a numbered program, press HOME, enter an O number, press ALTER, fill the Rename fields as needed, and press ENTER to save it. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes from the provided documentation:

- Hydraulic pressure is set below the recommended minimum (recommended minimum operating pressure is 120 psi). Low pressure may cause unreliable tailstock function. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- HPU oil level or temperature issues: HPU oil low or HPU oil temperature warning/overheat can affect hydraulic operation. Check HPU oil level and temperature. [003__L1__Chapter_3_Control_Icons__pp89-102.pdf]

- Loss of hold force after power interruption: If power was lost while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost and the workpiece must be supported and the tailstock zero returned before resuming. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock quill creep due to normal hydraulic leakage when left partially retracted or not bearing on a workpiece. Stow fully (press and hold foot pedal 5 seconds) to maintain retract pressure. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot pedal lockout setting: If Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut (Setting 332) is ON, the tailstock foot pedal is ignored. Verify Setting 332 is OFF. Also Setting 322 can generate an alarm if no part is found when using M21/foot pedal. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Note about controls: [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion—if you expected feed hold to stop tailstock motion you may need to press [RESET] or [EMERGENCY STOP]. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If these items do not explain the problem, the provided documents do not contain further troubleshooting steps.

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: The manual describes three methods for tool changes on Haas lathes and important precautions:

- Automatic/tool-changer types:
  - Auto (uses the machine’s automatic tool changer). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
  - Gang Tl (changes only tool offsets; e.g., T12 uses offset from tool 12, T1213 uses offset from tool 13, T1200 uses no tool offset). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
  - Tl Post (manual tool change): when a T-code tool change is executed the machine stops and prompts the operator to load the tool; after loading press [CYCLE START] to continue. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- G200 “Index on the Fly” (speed-optimized tool change):
  - G200 T... with optional U (relative X), W (relative Z), X (final X), Z (final Z) causes the turret to unclamp, move incrementally by U and W from its current position, complete the tool change, then rapid to the X,Z called on the G200 line. Example: G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2. . [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
  - CAUTIONS: proof the program at reduced rapid (5%), be careful when starting from the middle of a program; turret unclamps and moves slightly toward the spindle (.1–.2") when unclamped so do not have the tool directly against jaws/collet; U and W are incremental from the current position—if you have manually jogged, the incremental move could cause collisions (consider Setting 93/94 Tailstock Restricted Zone). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

- General notes and safety:
  - Use standard tool-change lines (e.g., G53 safe X/Z and Tnn) if not using G200. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
  - Setting 113 (Tool Change Method) selects which change method the machine uses (Auto, Gang Tl, Tl Post). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

If you want exact example code for a G200 tool change or the standard tool-change sequence, refer to the G200 example and the sample tool-change lines in 007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf.

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. There are multiple safety warnings and requirements specific to the chuck. Key points:

- Improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; higher speeds reduce chuck clamping force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Unsupported barstock must not extend outside the drawtube. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

QUESTION: I want to set the tool offsets of the HAAS Lathe. What parts/items do I need before I can start?
STUDENT ANSWER: The documentation states you must have the Automatic Tool Probe installed and calibrated before using the automatic tool-setting G-codes (G211/G212). Also, a tool must be called (Tnnn) before running G212 (or be present for G211 which requires T and H). Reference specifics:

- Automatic Tool Probe must be calibrated before using G211/G212. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- G211 requires a Tnnn and an Hnnn (tool and tool tip direction). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- G212 requires a previously called tool offset (Tnnn) before running or an alarm will be generated; care must be used to avoid collisions with back-working tools. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

If you plan to use manual tool setting (G211) you also need to be able to lower the probe arm and jog the tool tip into position per the procedure described. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

If you intended other tooling/setup items (probe hardware, correct T and H values, and calibration), those are the required items per the provided documents. If you need the detailed step sequence, that cannot be determined beyond these prerequisites from the provided excerpts.

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Run‑Stop‑Jog‑Continue lets you stop a running program, jog the X/Y/Z axes away from the part, and then resume the program.

Procedure summary:
- Press [FEED HOLD] — axis motion stops but the spindle continues to turn. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Press the axis key ([X], [Y], or [Z]) then press [HANDLE JOG]; the control stores the current X, Y, and Z positions and lets you jog (only X, Y, Z can be jogged in this mode). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Press [CYCLE START] to continue the program from the stored positions. (Implied by the feature name and interaction with [FEED HOLD]/[CYCLE START] on the pendant; see pendant controls and [FEED HOLD] behavior.) [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf]

Possible benefits (from described behavior):
- Allows the operator to pause motion and move the tool away from the workpiece for inspection, clearing chips, or checking setups without stopping the spindle. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Stores and restores axis positions so the program can resume accurately from the same point. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Limits jog capability to X/Y/Z only, reducing the chance of unintended axis motion while repositioning. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can back up the machine data and programs to a removable device (for example a USB memory device) or to the network using the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) and then remove rarely used programs from machine memory. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

How to do it (from the Device Manager):
- Press [LIST PROGRAM] to open the Device Manager; select the device tab for the destination (Memory, USB, or network). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]  
- Use the cursor keys to highlight the programs/directories to back up; press ENTER to place a check mark in the file selection box for each file you want to copy. (Check-mark selection lets you operate on multiple files at once.) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]  
- Press [F2] to start the copy operation, choose the destination device/directory, enter the destination directory (RIGHT arrow), then press ENTER to complete the copy. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Notes and tips from the documentation:
- File names and comments can be set when creating or saving programs so files on the backup device are identifiable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]  
- The active program is protected from deletion; ensure you select and back up any programs you plan to remove before deleting them from memory. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]  
- If you later reload a saved program from the backup device, use the Device Manager to copy it back into machine Memory (reverse the same copy steps). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

If you want offsets or other machine data included with saved programs, there is a setting that controls saving offsets with program files (so you can restore offsets when reloading). See Setting 156 for including offsets in saved program files. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

If you need guidance backing up macro variables or machine data beyond program files, macro/global variables and machine data can be saved/loaded via Net Share or USB similarly (refer to the Macros section for macro variable storage notes). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I power up the HAAS lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Before powering up, make sure possible crash areas (tool probe, parts catcher, tailstock, tool turret, secondary spindle) are clear. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]

Power-up procedure:
1. Press [POWER ON] until you see the Haas logo on the screen; after boot the startup screen appears (press [CANCEL] to dismiss). [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf]

4. If the machine is enclosed, close the doors. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__01__4.1_Machine_Power-On__pp103-103.pdf]  
5. Press [POWER UP]. The Zero All Axes display appears — select the axis zero return order. After this the control is in OPERATION:MEM mode and you can press [CYCLE START] to run the active program or use other control functions. - Find And Replace Text: open the editor pull-down menu (F1) → Search → specify the code to Find and optional Replacement, choose direction, then use:
  - F1 to find each occurrence,
  - F2 to replace the current occurrence,
  - F3 to step through find-and-replace for each occurrence,
  - F4 to Replace All (cannot undo). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__03__5.3_Tips_and_Tricks__pp147-150.pdf] [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

- Modify menu (bulk edits): use options such as “Remove All Line Numbers” or “Renumber All Lines”, and the “Reverse + And - Signs” function to change signs program‑wide. Note Modify operations automatically save and cannot be undone with UNDO, so save a copy first if needed. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

If you want to change blocks of lines at once, use Block Selection (F2) to select multiple blocks, then Delete, ALTER (move), or copy/paste the block. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes from the manual excerpts:

- Hydraulic pressure too low: recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; if set lower the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Loss of hold force after power interruption: if power was shut off or interrupted while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost and you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock to resume operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot pedal disabled by setting: Setting 332 (Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut) when ON causes the tailstock foot pedal to be ignored. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Tailstock control/pressure adjustments located at HPU: quill/hold force is controlled by hydraulic pressure at the HPU (except ST‑40 which uses Setting 241). Incorrect HPU valve settings can cause improper hold force. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage/creep: tailstock position can change over time if left partially retracted or not in contact with a workpiece due to normal hydraulic system leakage. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If none of the above apply, the provided documents do not give further troubleshooting steps.
