QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: The manual describes several tool-change methods and commands for Haas lathes; use T-codes (Tnn or Tnnnn) to call tools and use the machine’s tool-change method (automatic changer, gang turret, or manual post) as configured in Setting 113. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__03__5.3_Tips_and_Tricks__pp147-150.pdf] [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Key points and steps:
- Call the tool with a T code (e.g., T101). The T code may specify tool number and offset (Tnn or Tnnnn). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]  
- The control executes the tool change according to Setting 113 (Tool Change Method):  
  - Auto — uses the machine’s automatic tool changer.  
  - Gang Tl — changes only tool offsets (examples: T12 uses offset 12, T1213 uses tool 12 with offset 13, T1200 uses no offset).  
  - Tl Post — halts and prompts for a manual tool load; load tool then press [CYCLE START] to continue. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]
- G200 “Index on the Fly” can perform a faster tool change (unclamp, small incremental U/W move, tool change, then rapid back to commanded X,Z) — use with caution and proof-run at reduced rapid speed first. Example usage: G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2.; ensure tools/jaws won’t collide during turret unclamp movement. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

Additional operational notes:
- If using live tooling, the live-tool drive automatically turns off at a tool change. Clamp the spindle (M14/M114) for best milling accuracy before machining. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]  
- To set or update tool offsets use the Automatic/Manual Tool Setting cycles (G211/G212) with a calibrated tool probe; G211 requires a Tnnn and Hnnn; G212 requires a prior Tnnn call and correct H value. Use caution probing back-working tools to avoid crashes. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

If you need the exact program lines or an example program for your tool-change method (automatic, gang, manual, or G200), say which method you use and I will cite the specific example lines from the manual.

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The HAAS lathe chuck carries specific safety warnings: do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; unsupported barstock must not extend outside the drawtube; chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the chuck diameter; do not machine parts larger than the chuck; improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force; grease the chuck weekly and follow the chuck manufacturer’s service instructions; and hydraulic pressure must be set correctly to securely hold the workpiece without distortion. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

- Chuck installation/removal and additional chuck safety are referenced elsewhere in the index (see entries for “chuck…safety and” and “chuck…installation/removal”) for further procedures. [010__L1__Index__pp451-456.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I install a collet on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: To install a live-tool collet on the HAAS lathe, follow the Live Tooling Cutting Tool Installation steps:

- Insert the tool bit into the ER-32-AN nut insert, then thread the nut insert into the collet housing nut. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]
- Place the ER-32-AN tube wrench over the tool bit and tighten the ER-AN nut insert by hand using the tube wrench. Then place Spanner 1 over the pin and lock it against the collet housing nut; engage the tube wrench teeth with Spanner 2 and tighten. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

Caution: Never tighten the live-tool collets on the turret. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

Then, for mounting in the turret:
- Mount a radial or axial live tool holder, snug the mounting bolts, and torque them to 60 ft-lbs (82 N-m) in a criss-cross pattern, ensuring the bottom face of the toolholder is flush with the turret face. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

QUESTION: I want to change out a tool for a different one on the HAAS Lathe. How do I select the tool I want to switch out on the turret?
STUDENT ANSWER: To change to a different tool on the Haas lathe turret, use a T-code to select the next tool and offset (Tnnoo).

- Example: T101 selects tool 1, offset 1 (the code format is Txxyy, where xx is tool number and yy is geometry/offset). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]
- How to load/change tools:
  1) Power up/restart, then ZERO RETURN and ALL to move the turret to a normal position. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]
  2) Switch to MDI mode, then use TURRET FWD or TURRET REV to index to the next tool. The Active Tool window shows the current tool. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]

- Notes:
  - The Tnnoo format is T followed by tool number and offset number (e.g., T101 for tool 1, offset 1). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]
  - You can call a specific tool with a Tnnn code before the G211/G212 cycles, and the tool wear offset is applied as part of the code. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__05__5.5_Miscellaneous_Codes__pp155-156.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes and checks (based on HAAS tailstock documentation):

- Insufficient hydraulic pressure: Ensure the hydraulic pressure at the HPU is at or above the recommended level (minimum 120 psi) for reliable tailstock operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Lost hold force due to power interruption: If power was shut off or interrupted while the tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost. Zero return the tailstock after power is restored and resume operation as instructed. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock not engaged or in incorrect position: Make sure the tailstock is manually positioned and locked in place when using M21 (forward) or that you’re not issuing M22 (retract) commands while the tailstock is not properly retracted or held. The tailstock requires proper engagement to apply hold force. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Restricted zone collision risk: If the tailstock is within the Restricted Zone (set by Settings 93/94), it can trigger warnings or prevent motion to avoid collisions. Verify and adjust these settings and test limits after changes. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Pedal lockout or control settings: If the tailstock pedal is locked out or disabled, normal tailstock motion may be prevented. Check the Tailstock Foot Pedal LockOut setting (Setting 332) and related control options. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

- Specific tailstock type behavior: If you have ST-20/30 (hydraulic) or ST-40 (servo) tailstock, ensure you are following the correct startup and hold-force procedures for your model (e.g., adjusting hydraulic pressure for hold force; servo brake on power interruption for ST-40). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If the issue persists, provide details on which type (ST-10/ST-20/ST-30/ST-40) and what aspect isn’t functioning (forward hold, retraction, or quill movement) to narrow the cause. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The safety notes specific to the Haas Lathe chuck warn that improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force, and there are several chuck-specific precautions.

Key points include:
- Do not machine parts larger than the chuck; improper clamping can eject parts at high speed. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; higher speeds reduce clamping force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the diameter of the chuck. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Follow all chuck manufacturer’s warnings and ensure correct workholding procedures. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Ensure proper hydraulic pressure to securely hold the workpiece without distortion. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

QUESTION: I keep noticing my HAAS Lathe air reservoir has too much condensation in it. Is there any way to fix this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The condensate purge settings control how often and how long condensate is purged from the system air reservoir.

- Adjust Setting 243 (Air Water Purge On-Time) to change how long each purge lasts (seconds).

QUESTION: What are the risks/warnings I should be aware of when using the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion with the HAAS Lathe?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: You should not remove, or change out the offsets or tools while in this operation, due to the machine going back to the previous offsets when continuing, which could result in undesired collisions. You should also not expect or rely on the machine taking the same path back to the original position that you took away from it. The spindle is also still running in this mode, so it is not safe to interact with certain parts of the machine even if the axis motion has stopped.

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to back up and transfer programs and data to an external device (e.g., USB memory) or to another attached device on the control. This lets you archive rarely used programs off the machine while keeping current data intact. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

How to do it:
- Connect a USB memory device to the control pendant; the Device Manager will show the available memory devices as tabs. Select the USB tab to access files on the USB device. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- In the device list, highlight the programs you want to archive, then use the copy operation (press F2 or the Copy command) to copy them to the USB device (destination directory). You can run this on multiple selected files at once using the check-mark selection. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- After archiving, you can delete the archived-from locations on the machine to reclaim space, leaving active and frequently used programs in memory. The File Commands and Delete functionality let you remove selected files or directories once you have confirmed the operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Notes:
- The device manager is used to access, save, and manage data on the CNC control and attached devices, load/transfer programs between devices, set the active program, and back up machine data. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes to check:

- Hydraulic pressure too low. The recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; pressures below this can cause unreliable operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Hold force settings incorrect or not set for your model. For ST-20/30/ST-40, adjust the tailstock hold force via the appropriate setting (ST-40 uses Setting 241; ST-20/30 vary by model). If the hold force is insufficient, the tailstock may not engage properly. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Power interruption/reset issue. If power to the lathe is interrupted, hold force is lost and you must zero return the tailstock to resume. After restoration, you can resume only if there are no M22 commands in the program; otherwise edit the program to block tailstock motion. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Tailstock position or restricted-zone interaction. If Settings 93/94 (X/Y clearances) create a restricted zone, the tailstock may not operate as expected if the turret or tools encroach the zone. Verify the restricted zone settings and test limits after changes. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Manual vs. automatic positioning and pedal operation. Ensure the tailstock is properly locked in place when commanded forward (M21) or retracted (M22); incorrect manual positioning or pedal use can affect operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: To perform a tool change on a Haas lathe, use the G200 Index on the Fly method:

- Write a G200 line with the tool change: e.g., G200 Tnnn U.x W.y Xpos Zpos. The U and W values are the incremental X and Z offsets from the current tool position; Xpos Zpos specify the final turret/toolchange position after the change. Example from the manual: G200 T202 U.5 W.5 X8. Z2. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- Before the G200 line executes, the turret unclamps from its current position, then moves incrementally according to U and W, and completes the tool change at the new position. The turret then rapids to the XZ position called out on the G200 line. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]
- Note: The turret moves very quickly and increments relative to its current position, so avoid tailstock collisions by configuring Tailstock Restricted Zone (Settings 93 and 94). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

Additional context:
- If you’re turning from OD work, you do not need to return to a separate safe tool-change location; the G200 block handles the tool-change movement and offsets in one line. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

Safety note:
- When using G200, be aware that the turret unclamps and then moves incrementally; preview the program and test away from the chuck to ensure clearance. [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part02.pdf]

QUESTION: A client wants us to measure all out movements in MM instead of Inches. Can the HAAS Lathe also reflect this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. On the Haas lathe, set Setting 9 (Dimensioning) to MM to switch to millimeters.

- This changes programmed X and Z units to mm and converts offset values when changing from inches to mm. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]
- The default G-code also changes: G21 for MM (instead of G20 for INCH). [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]
- Note that changing the unit setting does not automatically translate an existing in-memory program; you must modify the programmed axis values for the new units. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: I keep noticing my HAAS Lathe air reservoir has too much condensation in it. Is there any way to fix this?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The Haas control includes condensate purge settings for the air reservoir.

- Use Setting 242 (Air Water Purge Interval) to specify how often condensate purges occur (minutes).
- Use Setting 243 (Air Water Purge On-Time) to specify how long each purge lasts (seconds).
- Adjust these values to increase purge frequency or duration as needed to reduce condensation. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part02.pdf]

Then lastly tighten the setscrew on the side of the spindle nose.

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: From the provided documents, the HAAS lathe tailstock relies on hydraulic pressure control via the HPU to hold and move the quill. If the tailstock isn’t functioning, potential causes include insufficient hydraulic pressure, or incorrect hold force settings, and the need to ensure the tailstock is properly engaged and not in a restricted zone.

Key points to check:
- For ST-20/30 hydraulic tailstock, ensure the hydraulic pressure is set correctly at the HPU to achieve the required tailstock hold force, with a recommended minimum of 120 psi for reliable operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Verify you are using the correct tailstock type (hydraulic quill, hydraulic positioned, or servo) for your lathe model, as operation varies by type. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- For ST-20/30, check that the tailstock hold pressure is active and that power to the lathe is stable; if power is interrupted, you may lose hold force and need to zero return after power is restored. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.3_Hydraulic_Tailstock_ST-20/30__pp109-110.pdf]
- Ensure the control is not preventing tailstock motion due to a restricted zone conflict or incorrect settings for tailstock X/Z clearance (Settings 93, 94) if you’re approaching the tailstock during operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.8_Tailstock_Restricted_Zone__pp111-112.pdf]
- If using the ST-40 servo tailstock, verify servo hold force via Setting 241 and that the tailstock is engaged; a power interruption may require resuming with caution after ensuring no M22 commands cause collision. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.4_ST-40_Servo_Tailstock_Operation__pp110.pdf]

If you can provide which tailstock type and model you have (ST-10/ST-20/30/ST-40) and any symptoms (no hold, no movement, leaks, alarms), I can narrow down the likely cause using the exact references above. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: From the provided HAAS manuals, check the following possibilities related to hydraulic tailstock issues:

- Ensure the tailstock hydraulic pressure is set correctly at the HPU to achieve the required hold force (ST-10, ST-20, ST-30, ST-40 variants). The startup and hold-force guidance says adjust hydraulic pressure at the HPU and refer to the machine decal for the correct setting. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- For ST-20/30 hydraulic tailstock, the recommended operating pressure is at least 120 psi; lower pressures may cause unreliable operation. If pressure is too low, the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- After a power interruption, the tailstock may lose hold force; you should zero return the tailstock to resume operation. The ST-20/30/40 tailstock procedure notes that if power is interrupted while engaged, hold force is lost and must be restored, with a zero return before starting a new cycle. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- For ST-40 servo tailstock, ensure the correct hold force is set via Setting 241 (Tailstock Hold Force is user-configurable); verify the hold force is within the specified range. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Note: The tailstock must be properly engaged (held against the part or at the retract/hold position) and the tailstock pedal behavior and restricted zone settings can affect operation; verify the tailstock is engaged correctly and that restricted zones are not triggering faults. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If none of these conditions explain the issue, the documentation provided does not specify additional troubleshooting steps beyond pressure, power restoration, and hold-position considerations. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

LwA sound power level A-Weighted levels will be 75.0dB or lower. 85dB is typically the audio level required for ear protection, but wearing ear protection is still recommended.

QUESTION: I want to set the tool offsets of the HAAS Lathe. What parts/items do I need before I can start?
STUDENT ANSWER: You need the tools and the offset/geometry data for each tool, plus the control commands to write offsets:

- Physical tools/inserts mounted and identified (e.g., a standard insert for each compensated tool). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]
- Tool nose radius for each turning tool (set the Tool Nose Radius offset; radius values are used for compensation). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]
- Tool tip direction code for each tool (specify the tip direction on the geometry offsets page). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]
- Tool length geometry and appropriate tool geometry offsets (set geometry offsets and clear length wear offsets as needed). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]
- Any required wear offsets cleared or prepared (clear Radius Wear and Geometry Wear offsets when fitting new tools; use wear offsets for small adjustments). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]
- Knowledge of how you will input offsets in the program or control (use G10 to set offsets within a program or enter offsets via the control’s offsets/geometry pages). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part01.pdf]

Supporting notes:
- Approach and departure moves must be planned when using Tool Nose Compensation (ensure space for these moves). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__xviii5.7.3_Using_Tool_Nose_Compensation__pp162-189_part01.pdf]
- If using G10 to program offsets, know which L and P codes apply (e.g., L2 for work coordinate origin, L10 for geometry). [007__L1__Chapter_7_G-codes__pp279-364__L2__01__7.1_Introduction__pp279-362_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?

- Only the X, Y, and Z axes can be jogged in this mode. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Safety reminder:
- Do not enter the machining area while the machine is in motion (motion may be possible when power is on); use appropriate caution when jogging with the spindle still turning. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

- You can only jog the X, Y and Z axes in this mode; the control stores current X, Y, Z positions before jogging — ensure you understand which axes will move and where the tool will be when you resume. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

- An axis or spindle over‑current condition can start an overload timer (starts at 1.5 minutes); if the overload persists, a SERVO OVERLOAD alarm will occur — be aware of potential overload/trip during motion. QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can offload programs and macro (variable) data to removable or network storage (USB or Net Share), then delete seldom-used programs from the machine. The control stores programs and macro variables on machine memory, USB, or Net Share so you can restore them later. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf] [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]

How to do this (concise steps):
- To save programs:
  - Use the Device Manager ([LIST PROGRAM]) to select the program you want to copy to external storage. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]
  - In the Program Editor you can use File → Save As or Set To Run / Save to write programs to the attached memory device (machine memory, USB, or Net Share). Press [MEMORY] to save and load into the Active Program pane. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]
  - For MDI-created code: press [HOME], type an O-number, press [ALTER], enter filename/title in the RENAME popup, then press [ENTER] to save to memory (and then copy to USB/Net Share as needed). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]
- To save macro variables (global macros, etc.):
  - Save or load macro variables through the Net Share or USB port (same method used for settings and offsets). Use the Macro Vars display to view/modify before saving. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]

Safety / operational notes:
- Macro variables #10000–#10999 (and legacy ranges) are persistent across power-off and can be saved/loaded via USB/Net Share; ensure you do not overwrite global variables used by factory-installed options. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]
- When restoring programs or macros, consider inserting G103 P1 at program start while debugging to limit look‑ahead buffering (the display may show variable values up to ~15 blocks ahead). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes from the manual:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum operating pressure for hydraulic tailstocks (ST-20/30) is 120 psi; below this the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Loss of power while engaged — if power was interrupted while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock to resume operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Incorrect operation sequence or configuration (ST-10) — on the ST-10 the tailstock body must be locked in place before commanding M21; also the quill cannot be moved with handle jog or ZERO RETURN/ALL. Using improper commands can cause unexpected behavior. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__11__5.10_Subprograms__pp191-191.pdf]

- Hydraulic leakage or check-valve behavior — tailstock position can change over time due to normal hydraulic leakage; M22 retracts then powers off and check valves hold the quill, and pressure is reapplied on Cycle Start or program loop to ensure retraction. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot-pedal or control settings — tailstock pedal control can be enabled/disabled with Setting 332; incorrect setting could affect pedal operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If these points do not explain the issue, the provided documents do not give further troubleshooting steps.

- A program tool change is typically triggered by an M06 tool‑change command in the program; the manual notes that Settings 83, 87 and 88 can make M30 and M06 (and [RESET]) return overridden values to defaults, indicating M06 is the program tool‑change mechanism. QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: You can copy the machine programs and machine data to removable media (USB) or to a network location and then delete the seldom-used programs from the machine; later you can restore them by copying them back. [004__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf] [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]

Recommended steps
- Plug in a USB memory device (or use Net Share).
- Press [LIST PROGRAM] to open the Device Manager. Select the device tab that contains the programs you want to back up. [004__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Mark files to copy by highlighting each program and pressing [ENTER] to place a check mark, or highlight a single file to copy just that file. [004__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- Press [F2] (Copy). In the Select Device popup choose the destination (USB or network) and use [RIGHT] to enter folders as needed. Confirm the copy by pressing [ENTER] in the Insert Directory: Copy popup. [004__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]
- To restore, repeat the copy procedure with the USB (or network) as the source and the machine memory as the destination. [004__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Other useful notes
- To save an ad-hoc program you typed in MDI into the program list: put the cursor at the start of the MDI program, enter an O number (Onnnnn), and press [ALTER]; then complete the Save popup. [005__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__02__5.2_Program_Edit_Modes__pp139-146.pdf]
- Macro variables and other offsets can be saved/loaded via Net Share or USB (similar to settings and offsets). Use this for global macro variables you want to preserve. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]
- If you delete programs from machine memory they are protected from accidental deletion while active; make sure you have confirmed successful copies before deleting. [004__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: The HAAS machine can do a full machine backup, which copies the settings, programs, and other data so it's easy to restore later on. To do this you can plug in a USB, navigate to it in the program list, press [F4] and select "Back Up Machine" in the appearing drop down menu. STUDENT ANSWER: You can copy the machine programs and machine data to removable media (USB) or to a network location and then delete the seldom-used programs from the machine; later you can restore them by copying them back. Recommended steps
- Plug in a USB memory device (or use Net Share).

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes from the documentation:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum for hydraulic tailstock (ST-20/30) is 120 psi; below this the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Incorrect HPU clamping/hold pressure setting — quill/hold force is controlled by HPU pressure; adjust at the HPU per the machine decal. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption while engaged — if power was lost while engaged the hold force is lost (ST-20/30) or servo brake state/position uncertainty (ST-40); after power restore special procedures (support workpiece, zero return or heed “Tailstock Force Restored” message) are required. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot pedal or control disabled/misconfigured — tailstock pedal control can be enabled/disabled with Setting 332 (and other tailstock foot-pedal behavior described); pressing the pedal during motion stops the sequence. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage/creep — tailstock position can change over time if left partially retracted or not in contact due to normal hydraulic leakage. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Incorrect use of ST-10 manual tailstock — on ST-10 you must position the body manually and lock it before commanding M21; the quill cannot be moved with HANDLE JOG or power-up/zero-return. Using M21/M22 incorrectly or without locking the body can cause problems. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf] 

- M-code/program issues — M21 (forward/hold) and M22 (reverse/retract) behavior and interaction with power-cycle/looping (M99) can affect hydraulic application; ensure program commands match the tailstock type and power/zero-return state. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__11__5.10_Subprograms__pp191-191.pdf] [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If these checks do not identify the problem, the exact cause cannot be determined from the provided documents and you should follow service procedures or contact your Haas service representative. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. Warnings specific to the chuck include (summary):

- Improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]  
- Do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; higher speeds reduce clamping force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]  
- Unsupported barstock must not extend outside the drawtube. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]  
- Chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the diameter of the chuck; do not machine parts larger than the chuck. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]  
- Grease the chuck weekly and keep it clean (follow manufacturer instructions). [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf][004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]  
- Hydraulic pressure must be set correctly—excess pressure or incorrect setting can damage the machine or inadequately hold the workpiece. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]  
- After power loss check the workpiece in the chuck/collet because clamping pressure can be reduced. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]  
- Do not attach dead length stops to the hydraulic cylinder (damage results). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]  
- The chuck is heavy—be prepared to use lifting equipment to support it during removal. Also, when removing the chuck clamp it before unfastening mounting screws to avoid damaging drawtube threads. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]

(References: the Safety chapter [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf] and Chuck/Collet Replacement [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf].)

QUESTION: If I want to make a backup of my HAAS Lathe ATM(Advanced Tool Management) information how do I do so?
STUDENT ANSWER: Use the Device Manager [LIST PROGRAM] backup functions to save the ATM data.

Quick method — Full Machine Backup:
- Press [LIST PROGRAM], navigate to the USB or Network device, press [F4], select Backup Machine and press [ENTER].  
- Highlight Advanced Tool Management (ATM) in the Restore/Backup popup and press [ENTER] (use [F2] to select all or [F3] to clear).  
- Press [F4] to save a HaasBackup(mm-dd-yyyy).zip containing ATM. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

Selected-data method — Backup only ATM:
- Insert a USB device (or ensure Net Share is set up), press [LIST PROGRAM], navigate to the USB device in Device Manager and open the destination directory.  
- Press [F4], choose the ATM menu option and press [ENTER]. Type a filename and press [ENTER]. The control creates an ATM file (filename.ATM). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

Notes:
- Full backup is saved as HaasBackup(mm-dd-yyyy).zip and includes ATM (ATM.ATM) inside the zip. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

QUESTION: I've noticed that the corners of my machined parts look too sharp on all my programs. Can I change this on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. Change Setting 85 (Maximum Corner Rounding) to adjust how the control rounds corners — a lower value reduces corner radius (more exact) and a higher value permits more rounding up to the tolerance value; the default is 0.05". [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

Additional notes:
- A Setting 85 value of zero makes the control act as if Exact Stop is active for each motion block. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]
- The control will slow feedrates around corners to meet the chosen tolerance; smaller tolerances can reduce feed speed. [009__L1__Chapter_9_Settings__pp387-450__L2__01__9.1_Introduction__pp387-429_part01.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: Run-Stop-Jog-Continue lets you stop a running program, jog the X, Y or Z axis away from the part, then restart the program. To use it: press [FEED HOLD] (axis motion stops, spindle continues), press [X], [Y] or [Z], then press [HANDLE JOG]; the control stores the current X, Y, Z positions. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Possible benefits (from the described behavior):
- Allows the operator to remove the tool or workpiece from potential collision without stopping spindle rotation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Stores current positions so the program can be resumed accurately after jogging. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]
- Enables quick recovery from an unexpected interference or to clear chips without aborting the run. (This follows from the function of stopping axis motion and jogging away as described.) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure set below the recommended minimum (recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi); if lower, the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged: hold force is lost when power is shut off or interrupted; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock to resume operation when power is restored. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock left at a non-fully-retracted or not-in-contact position: the position can change over time due to normal hydraulic system leakage. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot pedal or control logic disabled: Check Setting 332 (enables/disables tailstock pedal control) — if disabled, pedal control won’t operate. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

Additional operational notes that can affect behavior:
- [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion; you must press [RESET] or [EMERGENCY STOP] to stop it. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If these checks do not identify or resolve the issue, the provided documents do not give further troubleshooting steps; contact qualified service personnel. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes based on the HAAS documentation:

- Hydraulic pressure is set too low — recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; if set lower the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Loss of hydraulic hold force after a power interruption — if power was shut off while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, hold force is lost and you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock to resume operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock quill creeping or changing position over time due to normal hydraulic system leakage — leaving the tailstock partially retracted or not in contact can allow position change. Stow fully retracted (press-and-hold pedal 5 seconds) to maintain retract pressure. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- For ST-10 specific: tailstock is manually positioned and quill motion is hydraulic; the tailstock body must be locked in place before commanding M21 — if not locked, improper operation or collisions can occur. Also ST-10 quill cannot be moved by HANDLE JOG or Remote Jog — misuse may appear as non-function. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__11__5.10_Subprograms__pp191-191.pdf] [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Foot-pedal / control logic issues: if the foot pedal is used while in motion the tailstock stops and must be re-sequenced; also ensure Setting 332 (pedal enable) is appropriately set. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If these items do not explain the fault, the provided documents do not contain further diagnostic steps.

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?
STUDENT ANSWER: Yes. The HAAS Lathe chuck has multiple safety warnings and cautions, including:

- Improperly clamped or oversized parts may be ejected with deadly force. Do not machine parts larger than the chuck. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Do not exceed the chuck’s rated speed; higher speeds reduce chuck clamping force. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Chuck jaws must not protrude beyond the diameter of the chuck. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__01__1.1_General_Safety_Notes__pp23-29.pdf]
- Hydraulic pressure must be set correctly to securely hold the workpiece without distortion; incorrect pressure can damage the machine or inadequately hold the workpiece. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]

QUESTION: Are there any safety warnings associated with the HAAS Lathe chuck specifically?

QUESTION: If I want to make a backup of my HAAS Lathe ATM(Advanced Tool Management) information how do I do so?

  - For a selected-data backup: Press [LIST PROGRAM], select USB/Net Share and destination directory → press [F4] → choose the ATM menu option and press [ENTER] → type a filename and press [ENTER]; the file saved for ATM is filename.ATM. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

- Confirm the ATM file is included in the zip (ATM.ATM) or that the selected .ATM file is saved in your destination. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

QUESTION: The unused sockets of my HAAS Lathe turret keep getting dirty after use. How can I prevent this?
STUDENT ANSWER: The manual recommends keeping tools and the turret clear of chips and debris and using proper coolant/lubrication practices; specifically, configure and test the tailstock restricted zone and safe tool positions so tools/turret avoid collisions and chip accumulation, and keep the work area (including turret and unused tool pockets) clean and clear per normal safety/maintenance guidance. [002__L1__Chapter_2_Introduction__pp41-88__L2__02__2.2_Control_Pendant__pp47-86_part01.pdf] 

If you mean chip/contaminant buildup from coolant or machining, the manual warns to use proper machine coolant (water‑soluble, synthetic or synthetic‑based; do not use plain water, flammable, or straight mineral oil) and to maintain coolant concentration to avoid machine damage and hazards—proper coolant choice and maintenance will reduce leaks and contamination that can dirty turret sockets. [001__L1__Chapter_1_Safety__pp23-40__L2__06__1.6_Safety_Decals__pp34-40.pdf]

Note: The provided sources do not include a dedicated cleaning or turret‑socket protection procedure; for specific cleaning intervals, socket covers, or guards, that information cannot be determined from the supplied documents.

QUESTION: What are the risks/warnings I should be aware of when using the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion with the HAAS Lathe?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: You should not remove, or change out the offsets or tools while in this operation, due to the machine going back to the previous offsets when continuing, which could result in undesired collisions. The spindle is also still running in this mode, so it is not safe to interact with certain parts of the machine even if the axis motion has stopped.

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes and quick checks based on the manual:

- Hydraulic pressure too low or not set correctly: The tailstock hold force is set at the HPU, and a minimum of 120 psi is recommended for reliable operation. If pressure is below 120 psi, the tailstock may not function properly. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption or reset issues: If power to the lathe is interrupted while the tailstock is engaged, hold force is lost and you must restore power and re-check. After power restoration, you may need to zero return the tailstock before resuming with certain commands. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Incorrect tailstock type/settings (ST-40 servo tailstock): For servo tailstocks, ensure Setting 241 (hold force) is set within the specified range (1000–4500 lbf or 4450–20110 N). Incorrect setting can lead to improper hold force. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock not properly engaged or locked when commanded (ST-10/ST-20/30): For ST-10, the tailstock body must be locked in place before M21; for ST-20/30/ST-40 ensure proper engagement and that hydraulic hold is active. If not locked or engaged, quill motion may not function correctly. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Tailstock pedal control or restricted zone causing interference: If pedal control is disabled or methods crossing the restricted zone cause unexpected behavior, the tailstock may not move as expected. Check Setting 332 (enable/disable tailstock pedal control) and tailstock Restricted Zone settings (93 and 94) as applicable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If you can share which model (ST-10, ST-20/30, or ST-40) and what symptom you observe (no movement, no hold, leakage, etc.), I can point to the most likely cause from the same documentation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes and checks for a non-working hydraulic tailstock on the Haas lathe:

- Insufficient hydraulic hold pressure: The ST-20/30 tailstock requires a minimum recommended hydraulic tailstock operating pressure of 120 psi for reliable function. Verify the hydraulic pressure at the HPU and adjust to the correct value per the machine decal. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Incorrect tailstock state or not locked before M21: For forward motion (M21), the tailstock must be manually positioned and the tailstock body locked in place. If not locked, forward pressure may not be maintained. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Power interruption or hold force loss: If power is interrupted, hold force can be lost; you may need to zero return the tailstock or reset after power restoration. For ST-20/30 startup after interruption, follow the procedures to resume operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.3_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]
- Restricted or collision zone interfering with motion: Ensure the tailstock is not entering a restricted zone or colliding with tools; Setting 93 (X clearance) and 94 (Z/B separation) define a safe zone. If the tailstock crosses this zone, motion may be inhibited or flagged. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.8_Tailstock_Restricted_Zone__pp... PDF]
- For ST-40 servo tailstock: verify the hold force setting (Setting 241) is within the specified range; improper hold force can prevent proper engagement. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.4_ST-40_Servo_Tailstock_Operation__pp... PDF]

If these checks don’t reveal the issue, consult the machine’s decal settings and perform the standard reset/zero-return sequence before reattempting operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes and checks based on the provided manual excerpts:

- For ST-20/30/40 hydraulic tailstock, ensure the hydraulic pressure at the HPU is correct to achieve the required tailstock hold force. The recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; if lower, the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- If the tailstock is engaged with a workpiece on ST-20/30, ensure you press RESET or EMERGENCY STOP as FEED HOLD does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion during operation. Power interruptions require zero return and may necessitate re-establishing hold force after power is restored. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- On ST-10 (manual positioning with hydraulic quill), verify the tailstock quill is properly locked in place before signaling M21; improper locking can cause malfunction. Also be aware the quill is the only automatically moving part and is controlled by hydraulic pressure; ensure hoses and hydraulic pressure are correct. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__11__5.10_Subprograms__pp191-191.pdf] and [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- If using a servo tailstock (ST-40), verify Setting 241 (hold force) is configured correctly (between 1000 and 4500 lbf or 4450–20110 N depending on units). Incorrect hold force can result in improper tailstock engagement. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Note that the tailstock has a restricted zone (Settings 93 and 94) to prevent collisions with turret tools; if these settings are misconfigured, the tailstock may appear nonfunctional or cause warnings. Ensure 93 and 94 are set correctly for your setup, or cancel the restricted zone if not needed. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- If the machine power has been interrupted, the tailstock hold may be lost and you must restore power and follow startup procedures (e.g., zero return after power restoration and before resuming cycles). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

[004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If you need to run a different program, you would load or call the desired program and then start it (through the standard program start workflow). [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__06__5.5.3_Program_Stop_Commands__pp157-158.pdf]

QUESTION: I want to set the tool offsets of the HAAS Lathe. What parts/items do I need before I can start?
STUDENT ANSWER: - The Haas system uses tool offset data configured via macro variables and tool offset pages. Specifically, tool offsets and related geometry/wear data are accessed through macro variables such as #20000-#20999 (or #6001-#6250 for older machines) and the dedicated tool offset pages listed under the Macro/ATM sections [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf], [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part02.pdf].
- For tool nose radius, tool length, and wear offsets, use the Tool Nose Radius Offset and the corresponding Wear Offset data areas tied to each tool in the geometry offsets page, with macro access through the ranges #2000x and #50001-#50200 (tool type) as described in the Macro Variables and Tooling sections [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf], [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part02.pdf], [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__5.6_Cutting_G-codes__pp157-158.pdf].
- You’ll also need access to the relevant g-code/Macro system variables for reading or setting offsets (e.g., #5201-#5326 groups of work offsets and #5081-#5086 tool length compensation), as well as the ability to display and edit Macro Variables on the machine (Macro Vars page) [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf].

If you want a concise list of concrete prerequisites:
- Confirm you have access to the Haas Macro variables ranges for tool offsets (#20000-#20999 for settings, or #6001-#6250 for settings compatibility) and the Tool Offset page data structures, plus the Tool Nose Radius Offset and Wear Offset mappings [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part02.pdf].
- Ensure you know which tools will be used (tool numbers/offsets) so you can populate the corresponding tool offsets and nose radius wear data on the geometry offsets pages [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__08__5.6_Cutting_G-codes__pp157-158.pdf].
- Have access to the Current Commands Macro Vars page to view and edit Macro Variables for live debugging of tool offset values if needed [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf].

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: The Run-Stop-Jog-Continue feature on the Haas lathe lets you stop a running program, jog away from the part, then start the program again. It is described in the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue section (Chapter 4.13) and is activated by pressing FEED HOLD to stop, then moving axes with HANDLE JOG to resume jogging, and pressing CYCLE START to continue. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

Benefits (implied by the procedure and context):
- Allows safe interruption of a running program to reposition or inspect the setup before continuing.
- Enables continuing automatic motion after temporary manual repositioning, without resetting the program.
- Provides a quick method to pause and resume operation for troubleshooting or part verification. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__14__4.13_Run-Stop-Jog-Continue__pp136-136.pdf]

QUESTION: What are the risks/warnings I should be aware of when using the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion with the HAAS Lathe?
GROUND TRUTH ANSWER: You should not remove, or change out the offsets or tools while in this operation, due to the machine going back to the previous offsets when continuing, which could result in undesired collisions. You should also not expect or rely on the machine taking the same path back to the original position that you took away from it. The spindle is also still running in this mode, so it is not safe to interact with certain parts of the machine even if the axis motion has stopped.

QUESTION: My HAAS Lathe is running out of space, but I don't want to add a permanent storage device to it. What can I do to keep all the current machine information and programs stored somewhere so I can remove programs that are rarely used without fear? And how would I go about doing so?
STUDENT ANSWER: From the Device Manager documentation, you can transfer and back up programs and data to devices attached to the control (USB, net share, etc.), and manage which programs are active or stored on memory vs. removable devices. Use List Program to access the device manager, select a device tab, and copy or move programs between memory and external storage. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__03__5.3_Tips_and_Tricks__pp147-150.pdf] 

How to proceed (concise steps):
- Open the Device Manager by pressing LIST PROGRAM to view available memory devices (Memory, USB, net share).
- Create or select a destination on an external device, then copy or duplicate programs using the Copy/Paste or Copy Popup procedures described in the Device Manager sections.
- Use the Create New Program or Select Active Program options to manage which programs stay in machine memory vs. on external storage, ensuring inactive or rarely used programs are stored off the machine.
- To move or copy multiple programs, mark them with check marks in the file display and use the Copy operation to transfer to the chosen device. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__03__4.3_Device_Manager_(_LIST_PROGRAM)__pp104-111.pdf]

Notes:
- The macros/variables and settings sections explain how programs may reference macro data that can be preserved across sessions if stored on macro-capable global storage; ensure you back up macro definitions if needed. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__07__6.7_Macros_(Optional)__pp218-245_part01.pdf]
- Regularly back up the chosen external storage contents after transferring programs to preserve them when removing less-used items. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__03__5.3_Tips_and_Tricks__pp147-150.pdf]

If you need a minimal workflow, I can outline a step-by-step sequence using the Device Manager to offload a subset of programs to USB and then reindex or reassign the active program from memory. [005__L1__Chapter_5_Programming__pp139-192__L2__03__5.3_Tips_and_Tricks__pp147-150.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I install a collet on the HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: To install a collet on the Haas lathe, follow the Collet Installation steps in 4.7.4:
1) Thread the collet adapter into the drawtube.
2) Place the spindle nose on the spindle and align one of the holes on the back of the spindle nose with the drive dog.
3) Fasten the spindle nose to the spindle with six SHCS.
4) Thread the collet onto the spindle nose and align the slot on the collet with the set screw on the spindle nose, then tighten the setscrew. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]

- Specific warnings for chuck/collet safety interlocks and ensuring hydraulic pressure is set correctly; chucks can eject parts if not clamped properly. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__07__4.7_Chuck_and_Collet_Replacement__pp118-122.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: The Run‑Stop‑Jog‑Continue motion lets you stop a running program, jog the tool away, then return it and continue the program. Procedure summary:
- When the control shows Jog Away, use the jog handle or jog keys to move the tool away; you may command coolant ([AUX CLNT] or [COOLANT]), start/stop the spindle with spindle override keys, or release the tool to change inserts.  
- CAUTION: the control will use previous offsets for the return position, so changing tools/offsets while interrupted is unsafe and not recommended.  
- Jog to a position close to the stored position or to an unobstructed rapid path back, press [MEMORY] or [MDI], then press [CYCLE START]. The control displays Jog Return and rapids Y and Z at 5% back to where [FEED HOLD] was pressed, then returns X; pressing [FEED HOLD] during this motion pauses (Jog Return Hold) and [CYCLE START] resumes. The control does not follow the same path used to jog away. Press [CYCLE START] again to resume program operation. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

Possible benefits (as described/implied in the procedure):
- Allows inspection, minor adjustment, or insert change while the program is stopped (you can release the tool and command coolant or spindle).  
- Lets you move the tool to a safe/unobstructed position and return automatically to the stop point so the program can resume without restarting the program sequence.  
- Provides controlled, slowed return (Y and Z rapids at 5%) and the ability to pause/resume the return for safety. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure too low — recommended minimum operating pressure is 120 psi; lower pressure can make the tailstock unreliable. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption or loss of power while engaged — hold force is lost when power is interrupted; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock after power is restored. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage — the tailstock position can creep over time if left not fully retracted or not contacting a workpiece. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Control/command behavior — [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion; you must press [RESET] or [EMERGENCY STOP] to stop it. Also check that M21/M22 or foot-pedal sequences are being used as expected (hydraulic pressure is applied to retract then powered off; pressure is reapplied on Cycle Start and M99). [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

Also verify hydraulic pressure settings at the HPU and refer to the machine decal for the correct pressure/hold-force information. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: Performing a live-tool load/change (summary):

- The live-tool drive automatically turns off when a tool change is commanded. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

Toolholder mounting (radial or axial live tool):
- Mount the live tool holder and snug the mounting bolts.
- Torque the mounting bolts in a criss‑cross pattern to 60 ft‑lbs (82 N·m). Ensure the bottom face of the toolholder is clamped flush with the turret face. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

Cutting‑tool installation into ER‑32‑AN:
- Insert the tool bit into the ER‑AN nut insert and thread the nut insert into the collet housing nut.
- Place the ER‑32‑AN tube wrench over the tool bit, engage the nut‑insert teeth, and hand‑tighten the nut insert.
- Use Spanner 1 to lock against the collet housing nut (you may need to turn the nut to engage the spanner), then engage the tube wrench with Spanner 2 and tighten fully. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

Safety note:
- Never tighten the live tool collets while the live tool is on the turret — doing so will damage the machine. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

QUESTION: If I want to make a backup of my HAAS Lathe ATM(Advanced Tool Management) information how do I do so?
STUDENT ANSWER: To back up ATM (Advanced Tool Management) data you can use either a full machine backup or a selected-data backup:

- Full machine backup:
  1. Press [LIST PROGRAM].
  2. Navigate to the USB or Network Device and press [F4].
  3. Select Backup Machine and press [ENTER].
  4. Highlight ATM (check it) and press [ENTER] (use [F2] to select all if desired).
  5. Press [F4] to create a zip named HaasBackup(mm-dd-yyyy).zip that will include ATM. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

- Selected machine data backup (writes just the ATM file):
  1. Insert a USB drive (or ensure Net Share is set up) and navigate to USB in Device Manager.
  2. Open the destination directory and press [F4].
  3. Select ATM from the menu and press [ENTER].
  4. Type a filename and press [ENTER]; the file is saved as filename.ATM. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes include:

- Hydraulic pressure set too low (recommended minimum 120 psi); below 120 psi the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Loss of power while engaged: if power was interrupted while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost and the workpiece must be supported and the tailstock zero-returned before resuming. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage can allow the tailstock position to change over time if left partially retracted or not in contact with the workpiece. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Incorrect operation commands or controls: the quill is moved by M21/M22 or the foot pedal (and [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion); attempting to jog with handle or using unsupported controls will not move the quill. Verify you are using proper M-codes, foot pedal, and that Setting 332 (pedal enable) is correct. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

Also check the machine’s hydraulic power unit (HPU) pressure adjustment and follow the decal on the machine for quill hold force / hydraulic pressure information. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

QUESTION: How do I perform a tool load/change on a HAAS Lathe?
STUDENT ANSWER: - Command the turret tool change in the program or via the control (a tool change will automatically turn off the live‑tool drive). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

- Install the cutting tool into the ER‑AN nut insert, thread the insert into the collet housing nut, hand‑tighten with the ER‑32‑AN tube wrench, lock Spanner 1 against the collet housing nut, then engage the tube wrench with Spanner 2 and tighten. Never tighten live‑tool collets while the toolholder is on the turret (this will damage the machine). [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

- Mount the axial or radial live tool holder to the turret, snug the mounting bolts, then torque the mounting bolts in a criss‑cross pattern to 60 ft‑lbs (82 N·m). Make sure the bottom face of the toolholder is clamped flush with the face of the turret. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

- For best milling accuracy after a tool change, use the spindle clamp M‑codes (M14 for main spindle, M114 for secondary spindle); the spindle will automatically unclamp when a new main spindle speed is commanded or [RESET] is pressed. Maximum live‑tool drive speed is 6000 RPM. [006__L1__Chapter_6_Options_Programming__pp193-278__L2__06__6.6_Live_Tooling__pp215-217.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: The Run‑Stop‑Jog‑Continue sequence described is the procedure used when you stop a program with Feed Hold, jog the tool away, then return and resume the program. Steps (summarized from the source):

- Press Feed Hold to stop; the control displays "Jog Away." Use the jog handle or jog keys to move the tool away (you may command coolant with [AUX CLNT] or [COOLANT], start/stop the spindle with spindle override keys, or release the tool to change inserts). CAUTION: restarting the program uses the previous offsets for the return position, so changing tools/offsets while interrupted is unsafe and not recommended. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

- Jog to a position near the stored position or to a position with an unobstructed rapid path back to the stored position. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

- Press [MEMORY] or [MDI] to return to the run mode that was active when you stopped; then press [CYCLE START]. The control displays "Jog Return" and rapids Y and Z at 5% back to where you pressed [FEED HOLD], then returns X. If you press [FEED HOLD] during this motion it pauses ("Jog Return Hold"); press [CYCLE START] to resume. The control does not follow the same path you used to jog away. When the jog‑return motion finishes the control goes into a feed‑hold state again; press [CYCLE START] to resume the program. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

Possible benefits (implied by the procedure in the source):
- Allows clearing the work area (jog away) for inspection, tool changes, or to remove obstructions before resuming. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]
- Provides a controlled, low‑speed (5% rapids) automatic return to the interruption point, reducing risk of collision on return. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

If you change tools or offsets while interrupted, the document cautions this is unsafe because the control uses the previous offsets for the return position. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf]

QUESTION: If I want machine-specific information about my HAAS Lathe's functions and do not want to use the internet, what can I do?

QUESTION: My hydraulic tailstock isn't functioning properly on the HAAS Lathe, what might be the cause?
STUDENT ANSWER: Possible causes noted in the documentation:

- Hydraulic pressure set too low: Recommended minimum hydraulic tailstock operating pressure is 120 psi; if set lower, the tailstock may not function reliably. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Power interruption while tailstock engaged: If power was shut off or interrupted while the hydraulic tailstock was engaged, the hold force is lost; you must support the workpiece and zero return the tailstock to resume operation when power is restored. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Normal hydraulic leakage over time: The tailstock position can change if left partially retracted or not in contact due to normal hydraulic system leakage. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Feed Hold does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion: During operation, pressing [FEED HOLD] does not stop hydraulic tailstock motion; you must press [RESET] or [EMERGENCY STOP] to stop it. (This can affect perceived operation.) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

If you need troubleshooting steps (pressure check, power-cycle/zero return, or HPU adjustment), the document gives these causes and related procedures. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__12__xvii4.11.1_Tailstock_Types__pp130-134.pdf]

- Press [LIST PROGRAM]. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

- In the Backup Machine pop-up, highlight ATM (Advanced Tool Management) and press [ENTER] to mark it; you can use [F2] to select all or [F3] to clear. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

If using the Selected Machine Data Backup menu instead:
- Select the ATM menu option, type a filename in the Save As pop-up, and press [ENTER]; the created file will be filename.ATM. [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__04__4.4_Full_Machine_Backup__pp112-115.pdf]

QUESTION: What is the Run-Stop-Jog-Continue motion on the HAAS Lathe? And what are the possible benefits of it?
STUDENT ANSWER: The document describes a Run‑Stop‑Jog‑Continue sequence (Jog Return) where, after stopping a program with Feed Hold, you jog the tool away and then return to run mode so the control rapids back to the point where Feed Hold was pressed and the program resumes.

Key steps and behavior:
- After Feed Hold the control displays "Jog Away"; you use the jog handle or jog keys to move the tool away (you may command coolant, start/stop spindle, or release tool to change inserts) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].
- Jog to a position near the stored position or to a position with an unobstructed rapid path back to the stored position [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].
- Press MEMORY or MDI to return to the same mode that was active when you stopped the program, then press CYCLE START; the control shows "Jog Return" and rapids Y and Z at 5% back to the position where Feed Hold was pressed, then returns X (pausing if Feed Hold is pressed during motion) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].
- Press CYCLE START again and the program resumes operation; note the control does not follow the same path you used to jog away, and the control uses previous offsets for the return position (so changing tools/offsets during an interrupt is unsafe and not recommended) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].

Possible benefits (implied by procedure):
- Allows safe removal or servicing (e.g., change inserts) while program is stopped, then resume without full program restart [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].
- Provides a controlled rapid return at reduced speed (5%) to the interruption point, reducing risk of collision on return [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].

Safety cautions:
- Do not change tools or offsets when you interrupt a program because the control will use previous offsets for the return position (unsafe and not recommended) [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].
- The control will not follow the same path you used to jog away, so ensure you jog to a position with an unobstructed rapid path back [004__L1__Chapter_4_Operation__pp103-138__L2__15__4.14_More_Information_Online__pp137-138.pdf].
